newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan Jul long-term prime seen cut to 2.7% - bankers.
newsitem.headline: Japan Jul long-term prime seen cut to 2.7% - bankers.

text.p: Japan's July long-term prime lending rate is likely to be set at 2.7 percent, down from 2.9 percent for June, sources at long-term credit banks said on Monday.
"Judging from today's market conditions, the long-term prime rate is likely to be cut by 0.2 percentage point," said an official at a long-term credit bank.
The Industrial Bank of Japan Ltd's (IBJ) 2.0 percent June five-year debentures were traded at 1.79 percent on Monday, traders said.

The prime rate is customarily set 0.9 percentage point above the coupon rate of the IBJ's monthly issued five-year debentures, the benchmark in Japan's debenture market from which these banks raise funds.
The prime rate is applied to loans of one year and longer to Japanese long-term credit banks' most creditworthy clients.
The long-term prime rate is reviewed every month, to reflect market trends.
IBJ will announce the coupon rate for its July five-year debentures and its new prime rate on Tuesday.

The other two long-term credit banks, the Long-Term Credit Bank of Japan Ltd and Nippon Credit Bank Ltd, are expected to announce the terms for their July debentures and new long-term prime rates on Wednesday.
